paragraphs.core_text: Love is the Father of Greatness, who dwells in his glorious land. The entirety of the divine has been revealed [there]in! These two are a single living body, the Father and his love; because he has given himself for every thing, as he exists in his aeons. Indeed, due to this, they called the Father, the Lord of the totality, 'love'. For he gave the victory to his aeons and his limbs.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure cosmological-correspondential mapping: Love → Father of Greatness → his land → his aeons. Both sides of every mapping stay within the cosmic system. 'These two are a single living body' is a body-unity formula mapping divine quality to divine being. 'They called' uses the impersonal naming formula characteristic of the substrate teaching voice. No contemporary references or institutional vocabulary.

Clear editorial extension of the ¶2 substrate pattern to the Manichaean church. The editor mimics the 'single body' formula ('the Mind and the church, a single body') and applies it to the apostle and church. Contains NT citation (John 15:13: 'There is no love greater than this...'). The phrase 'the church here' and 'the apostle too shall give his self for his church' locate the teaching in institutional present. Institutional score of 16.0 confirms. This is precisely the pattern-mimicry editorial seam: the cosmic teaching about Love/Father was complete at ¶2, and the editor added one more iteration applying it to the church.

paragraphs.core_text: What, conversely, is hate? Hate is the first death that welled up. It revealed the land of Darkness. This one called 'hate', because it has ruined all its perdition's offspring; it sinned even against a power foreign to it, and ruined it. Due to this they shall call it 'hated'; for it has caused destruction, both wounding in flesh, and what is not its own.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'Once again he speaks:' — formulaic dialogue frame attribution.
paragraphs.temporal_note: The seam flag is a false positive — institutional vocabulary is 0.0 and the content is purely cosmological. The teaching maps Hate → first death → land of Darkness. 'A power foreign to it' refers to the Light attacked by Darkness — core cosmological narrative. 'They shall call it' uses the impersonal naming formula. The binary structure (Love ¶2 / Hate ¶4) is the teaching architecture. 'Wounding in flesh, and what is not its own' describes the cosmic aggression of Darkness against the foreign Light substance.

paragraphs.core_text: Today again it causes wounding and destruction in all flesh. It kills them all with diverse deaths; these that are displayed today in every thing, in every type. Even the Cross of Light, the living soul, likewise too it ruins and kills them; as it did at the start. Indeed, due to this have they called it 'hated', this one from the hated; the envy from the envy; the devil from the devil; the bad that came about from the bad.
paragraphs.temporal_note: The 'today' language describes the cosmic middle-time (the epoch of mixture), NOT specific contemporary institutions. Both sides of the mapping stay within the cosmic system: Hate → wounding/destruction → 'all flesh', 'every thing', 'every type' — these are cosmic generalities, not institutional identifications. Compare with editorial bridge markers ('reigns today in the principalities') which point to specific institutions. 'As it did at the start' explicitly links present cosmic process to the primordial attack — this is the first-time/middle-time temporal structure of the cosmological teaching. 'Cross of Light' and 'living soul' are core substrate terms. The derivation chain at the end ('the hated from the hated; the envy from the envy; the devil from the devil; the bad from the bad') is a distinctive substrate formula mapping ontological origin through correspondential derivation.
